message.content:
VOTE: APPROVE

I was wrong on the origin sets. The brief’s “different origin sets / own base rates” sentence is the unpaired full-monthly contrast (591 vs 198). `parret_tyndet_vs_kvartal` is a different object: m%3==0 scored from `wf_monthly` on the same 198 quarter-end origins, 0 label disagreements, shared base rate 16.16% and baseline log-loss 0.4423, gap −1.02 pp, 10–90% [−4.47, +1.32]. That is the paired diagnostic. Citing it meets the veto.

Reservations (non-blocking):

1. Acceptance of §3.2(b) is conditional on `v5/analyser/frekvensgate_resultat.json` being in the same push as RAADETS_2027.md, with those fields and seed 42 intact. A secretary citation without the file is not evidence. Rasmus hash-checks it against the independent verifier before the push.

2. §3.3 must pin the penalty, not merely “include normalisation.” Under a summed loss, λ = 1 on ~800 rows is about one-third the per-observation penalty of λ = 1 on 267 (E2: β −1.29 → −1.41 per pp; P at +1.12 is 14.9% → 14.4%). Seal either λ_monthly = 1 × (N_m/N_q) or mean log-loss with λ scaled by 1/N_q. An unpinned spec confounds frequency with shrinkage in the unscored column.

3. §3.2’s “written gate passed; council declines to apply it” must not be read as the pre-run ablation3 gate having passed. That gate failed, 26.03 vs 26.05. The override is of the unpaired written reading, justified by (a)–(d) plus the paired −1.02 pp, not by a passed executed test.
message.reasoning:
I am preparing to vote as Grok 4.7.

I am re-examining my prior rejection of §3.2(b). The secretary claims the thinned monthly and quarterly origin sets are identical. I must verify whether this resolves the E2 score discrepancy before deciding to approve or reject.

The Fable Round 3 test has not been run. The interval [−4.47, +1.32] is absent from the brief. I will not ratify an unverified interval or a relabelled thinned gap to override a preregistered gate.

I am drafting a replacement for §3.2(b). It will state the thinned monthly score of +26.03 % versus the quarterly score of +27.05 % (−1.02 pp), clarify this is not a paired same-origin comparison, and delete the [−4.47, +1.32] interval unless a sealed E2 artifact is cited. I am also verifying the secretary's JSON path `v5/analyser/frekvensgate_resultat.json` and its episode-block bootstrap parameters.

The JSON confirms the thinned and quarterly origin sets are identical. Both contain 198 origins with matching pooled base rates and baseline log-loss. The script explicitly states this pairing is equivalent to the ablation3 setup. Therefore §3.2(b) is a valid paired same-origin comparison.

An independent verifier reproduced the paired comparison using ablation3's `wf_monthly`. The unpaired full-monthly comparison spans 591 origins against 198. §3.2(b) now cites the artifact and confirms verified origin identity. §3.3 adds that the sealed specification re-runs this same-origin diagnostic on the 2027 panel, with origin-set and label identity checked in code; its outcome is unknown at sealing.

The other two thinning phases pass with +32.13 % and +29.58 %. The full monthly and quarterly models are scored on different origin sets with separate pooled base rates. The brief notes that thinned-minus-quarter differences range from −1.0 to −3.1 percentage points, which is narrower than the MDE of 4.4–8.5.

My prior objection was wrongly applied to the thinned comparison. The brief's claim about different origin sets and pooled base rates concerns the full monthly versus quarterly fit, not the thinned versus quarterly fit.

The script note explicitly confirms the thinned monthly and quarterly origin sets are identical. This resolves my prior objection to §3.2(b). However, the artifact still introduces the [−4.47, +1.32] confidence interval, which was absent from the brief. I will not ratify an unverified interval as a reason for overriding the preregistered gate.

The artifact path and parameters are now explicitly cited. I am skeptical of the secretary as an interested party, but the verification is specific and falsifiable.

The artifact now shows the origin identity that Fable and Kimi had only asserted. The prior concern was mischaracterization, not unknownness. Because the result was already computed and is in the E2 artifact, it is treated as known under the ground rules.

The artifact-cited pairing satisfies the veto condition. The confidence interval is now anchored to a reproduced verifier artifact rather than an unverified claim. The specific Danish note and identical base rates provide strong evidence of correct origin identity. I am weighing these factors in deciding whether to approve.

The monthly walk-forward scored at quarter-end origins still compares a monthly fit against a quarterly fit on the same score origins. The other items are already accepted. I will approve.

The artifact path must be committed with RAADETS_2027.md. Otherwise the citation is hollow.

§3.2 still claims the written gate passed before stating it was declined. DeepSeek's framing is more accurate: the executed pre-run gate failed, and the literal reading compares different models. I will not block this override sentence, but the wording overstates commensurability.

I will reserve that the sealed specification must pin the loss/penalty normalisation precisely. It should fix λ_monthly to λ_quarterly scaled by N_m/N_q or to the mean loss, rather than leaving it vague. Otherwise the unscored column would conflate frequency with shrinkage.

The loss/penalty normalisation must be explicitly specified rather than discovered. The power clause remains valid until §6.2 is established. Rasmus should confirm the JSON file hashes match before the document is pushed.

The 10–90 % interval [−4.47, +1.32] is internally consistent with the −1.02 percentage point gap and a standard deviation of 2.58. The pooled base rate 16.16 % equals exactly 32 out of 198 origins.

The loss/penalty normalisation must be pinned to an exact scaling rule. λ=1 on 800 versus 267 origins yields different estimators (β −1.41 vs −1.29, P 14.4 vs 14.9). The 2027 re-run is already in §3.3.
